newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close up but off highs.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed up but off highs on Tuesday following rises in selected market heavyweights and many secondaries, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 6.27 points, or 1.09 percent, to close at 580.21 points after hitting an intra-day high of 581.33 points in late afternoon trade.
Losers led gainers by 39 to 37, with 36 counters unchanged.
Some foreign buying of fundamentally-sound stocks could lend a positive tone on Wednesday as the market is back to normal conditions, said a foreign broker.
Brokers said trade was slow in the morning session as the market lacked fresh leads but some fresh buying of heavyweights in afternoon trading had pushed the composite index up.
Market heavyweights Telkom, cigarette maker Gudang Garam and cement producer Semen Gresik were among the targets of foreign buying, brokers said.
Telkom was up 100 rupiah to 3,700 rupiah on a turnover of about four million shares.
"Some foreign investors are switching their portfolio from Indosat to Telkom," said Kian Guntur, a trader with PT Schroeders Indonesia.
He said investors were making the switch due to reports that some analysts had downgraded recommendations on satellite firm PT Indosat.
Cigarette maker Gudang Garam rose four percent, or 350 rupiah to 9,100 rupiah on a volume of 225,000 shares on what brokers said was a technical rebound on cheap prices.
Property firm Duta Pertiwi topped the active list with 17.4 million shares changing hands. It gained 150 rupiah to 1,975 on market talk of a possible link-up with foreign partner.
Multifinance firm Gajah Surya rose 100 rupiah to 1,375 on 5.5 million shares.
Brokers ascribed the rise to recent shareholder approval to acquire 51.8 percent of Bank BDNI. BDNI rose 50 rupiah to 1,725 rupiah on a volume of 6.5 million shares.
Agriculture-related firm Smart Corporation of the Sinar Mas Group rose 125 rupiah to 1,800 rupiah on a turnover of 2.9 million shares.
Brokers said it was due to market talk that Salim Group, another conglomerate, could acquire the firm. Smart Corporation officials denied the rumours.
Textile firm Pan Brothers Tex rose 175 rupiah to 2,450 on a turnover of 2.7 million shares. Brokers said the rise was due to talk of a possible stock split.
